evidence.title: World's longest rivers | Description & Facts | Britannica
evidence.full_text: Accurate comparable river-length measurements, however, are often difficult to obtain, because stream definitions and measurement standards vary between countries. It is possible that the main channels of well over 100 of the greatest rivers may exceed 1,600 km (about 1,000 miles) in length. Measuring from the headwaters of the most distant source, the five longest rivers in the world are the Nile (in eastern and northeastern Africa), the Amazon–Ucayali–Apurímac (in South America), the Yangtze (in China), the Mississippi–Missouri–Red Rock (in the United States), and the Yenisey–Baikal–Selenga (in northern Asia). |rank |name |length* |(km) |(miles) |*Figures based on official sources. In countries where the metric system is used, conversions are from kilometres to miles

" It may be more straightforward to trace the source of other rivers, Johnston notes, but "the Amazon, by far the largest river in the world, is not so simple. evidence_refs.reasoning: Poses the question 'How long is the Amazon River?', implying its length can be measured.
Provides a specific length for the Amazon River: 3,976 miles (6,400 km).
Discusses tracing the source of the Amazon River, implying its length can be measured.
Mentions that comparable river-length measurements can be difficult due to varying standards, but implies that measurements are possible for other rivers.
Ranks rivers by length, implying that the lengths of other rivers can be measured.
Refers to the 'world's third-longest river', implying lengths of other rivers are measured.

elements.uncertainty: While evidence suggests other rivers' lengths can be measured, it does not provide a comprehensive list or confirmation that all other rivers' lengths have been measured and compared.

evidence_refs.reasoning: States the Amazon River 'only narrowly loses the title for the world's longest river to the Nile River'.
States that 'Nile is the longest river globally, while Yangtze is the third longest' and the Amazon is the second-longest.
Lists the Nile River as the longest (6,695 km) and the Amazon River as the second longest (6,400 km).
Lists the Nile as one of the five longest rivers in the world, without explicitly stating the Amazon is longer.
